## How to read this file

**The status vocabulary, used identically in both parts.**

| Label | Means |
|---|---|
| **FIXED 2026-08-18** | Changed in the working tree, and the change was found in `git diff` and re-read in the current source while writing this document. Both presets compile at `/W4` with zero warnings. **Not played.** |
| **PARTIAL** | Part of the finding is closed. The remainder is named, here, in the same row. |
| **NOT FIXED - BY DECISION** | Deliberate. The reason is recorded in §D and usually also in a comment at the site. |
| **OPEN** | Nothing changed. Live in the tree today. |
| **CLAIMED, NOT FOUND** | An agent recorded the fix as landed; this document went looking and could not find it. §F lists all four. |
| **HISTORY** | Describes the tree as it was on 2026-08-17. Line references are stale. |

**What "fixed" is worth here, stated once so it is not asked again.** Every fix in §B was verified
*statically*: the diff was read, the current source was re-read, and the file references below were
re-derived from the working tree rather than copied from the finding that reported them. **No human has
played any of it.** The project's own standing warning applies with full force - "both presets clean,
zero validation errors" proves the program starts and does not crash, and says nothing about whether a
per-block table is right, whether a screen conserves items, or whether a model looks like the thing it
is named after. §G says what the four checkers actually prove.

## A. What happened on 2026-08-18, and what it proves

**Method.** The whole tree was partitioned into 21 exclusive areas - three files too large for one
reader (`Creature.cpp`, `Block.hpp`, `Main.cpp`) were split by line range - and one read-only survey
agent was given each, with the project's own list of recurring bug shapes as the hunting brief. Findings
went into a SQL ledger with `duck / severity / confidence / owner_file / locus / summary / status`, so
that the fix wave could be batched by **owning file** rather than by subject. **128 findings** were
recorded. **16 fix agents** then worked in parallel on disjoint file sets - one owner per file, the only
hard constraint, because two agents editing one file loses work. **8 verification reviewers** read the
resulting diff afterwards and found further faults, which were fixed in turn (§C).

**Size of the change.** 96 files, **+18,190 / -4,075** lines measured at the end of the round. The fix
wave's own contribution was 89 files and +15,311 / -3,446; the remainder is the verification wave and the
documentation. The source tree is now **138 files / 77,146 lines**, with `Creature.cpp` at 10,110,
`Block.hpp` at 9,299 and `Main.cpp` at 9,180. There are **626 `static_assert`s** in the tree.

**Acceptance bar reached.** Both presets build clean at `/W4` with zero warnings.
`tools\check-models.ps1` 2629 matched / 0 disagreeing (3230 drawn, 271 with no model: 202 block
entity, 69 face template, 0 unfound), plus 359 `Model` blocks compared box for box and 95 `uv`
rectangles, both 0. `tools\check-ui-data.ps1` clean.
`tools\check-index.ps1` 704 entries / 0 wrong. Encoding clean.

**Ledger outcome.**

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Findings recorded | 128 |
| Marked `fixed` by the agent that took them | 120 |
| Left `open` in the ledger | 8 (§E.1) |
| Verified present in the tree by this document | 116 |
| **Claimed as fixed and NOT found in the tree** | **4** (§F) |
| Verified but only partly closed | 9 (marked PARTIAL in §B) |

**The ten that mattered most, in one line each.**

1. **An unbounded item-duplication exploit.** The inventory drag sweep survived `closeScreen`, which had
   already handed the cursor stack back to the inventory, so the next screen to open re-materialised it.
   Sixty-four cobble in, a hundred and twenty-seven out, repeatable as fast as a screen can reopen.
2. **A truncated save could replace a good one.** All six writers checked the stream *before* the
   destructor flushed it, then renamed the temp over the real file.
3. **`saveIfModified` cleared the dirty flag on failure**, so a chunk whose write was refused was never
   retried and was dropped outright when it unloaded.
4. **The ender chest was never saved at all.** It belongs to the player, not to a block, which is exactly
   why every block-entity table missed it.
5. **Creatures were the last unswept mover in the project** - one Euler jump and a destination-only
   overlap test, so a small mob that cleared a floor in a single step fell through the world off a ~13 m
   drop.
6. **A creature hurt by something it could no longer reach froze for up to 600 s**, because the held
   target was dropped past the leash and the threat id was not.
7. **The biome table had a hole.** Hot, wet, un-eroded land was claimed by no row and fell to a
   nearest-box metric.
8. **Bamboo was truncated at y 31.** Multi-block plants stopped at the chunk ceiling and the chunk above
   never finished the stalk.
9. **Rain's ground-contact fade only worked in the middle of the screen** - a radial distance was
   compared against a view-axis depth.
10. **Thirteen sound event banks were decoded at startup and never played**, because nothing in `game/`
    ever named the event.

**What this round did not do.** Nothing was played. No milestone was started. `main()` is not smaller -
it is larger, at roughly 8,000 lines from `Main.cpp:1102`. There is still no automated test suite and no
`selftest=1` startup pass; what exists instead is 626 compile-time assertions, which is table totality
for free and is **not** stack conservation.

## B. Fixed 2026-08-18, by system

Every row was re-read in the working tree. `file:line` is current as of 2026-08-18.

### B.1 Items, inventory and containers

| What a player saw | What changed | Where it is now |
|---|---|---|
| **Unbounded duplication.** A drag sweep armed in one screen survived the close and was rewound into the next screen's cursor | `cancelDrag()` is the single owner of the sweep and is called **first, unconditionally**, at the top of `closeScreen`; it commits rather than rewinds, because rewinding needs a `SlotHit` resolved against a screen that is no longer open | `Main.cpp:3355` (`cancelDrag`), `:3476` (call), `:3468-3473` (the falsifying edit is named: move it below the give-back and the bug returns), `:4506` (Q-throw) |
| A worn tool came out of a hopper new; a stowbox came out empty | The hopper stopped building a stack by hand; `slots::moveOne` is now the primitive | `SlotOps.hpp:81`, `SlotOps.cpp:41`, call site `Main.cpp:3077` |
| Room-for-these-items was answered by two functions that disagreed about `damage` | `ItemStack::space()` deleted repo-wide; every caller routes through `slots::roomFor` | tombstone `Item.hpp:1812-1821`; callers `Furnace.cpp:74`, `Inventory.hpp:67,104`, `Main.cpp:5133` |
| Craft-to-cursor merged a crafted stowbox onto a held one and one set of contents vanished | Both craft paths compare `damage` | `Main.cpp:5127-5135`, shift path `:5106-5111` |
| A recipe consumed the wrong stowbox or the wrong-wear tool | `Inventory::count`/`consume` take a `damage` argument defaulting to "any" | `Inventory.hpp:24-27`, `Inventory.cpp:23,33-39` |
| A bad hit test could write past the 36th slot | Bounds check | `Inventory.cpp:7-12` |
| Beds, signs and banners stacked to 64; the void eye to 16 | Bed 1, sign/hanging sign/banner 16, void eye 64, compass 64, written book 16 | `Item.hpp:1762-1806`, asserts `:1831-1841` |
| Fifteen music discs carried Mojang's track names and could never be played; three brewing reagents duplicated their own coined ids | Both duplicate runs deleted, with a two-stage save migration | `Item.hpp:26` (`kMusicDiscs = 22`), `:358-364`, migration `:1126`/`:1139`/`:1209` |
| A full bag silently destroyed a bucket, a cauldron swap, composter bone meal or a glass bottle | One `giveOrDrop` lambda: add, then drop the remainder, carrying `damage` | `Main.cpp:3567-3577`; callers `:6480, :6580, :6680, :6763, :6858` |
| A stowbox's handle was allocated even when the carrying item never spawned | The handle is allocated only if the box has contents, and it then *forces* the drop | `Main.cpp:6350-6354`, gate `:6408-6410`; blast twin `:8291, :8324-8325, :8367-8377` |

**New proofs.** `Inventory.hpp:205` `inventoryAnswersAgree()` - ten cases including a worn coal stack and
a stowbox at two damages; falsified by making `hasRoomFor` compare `item` alone. `SlotOps.hpp:49-60` -
falsified by writing `kMaxStack` for an empty slot or dropping the `damage` clause.

## C. Found by the verification pass, after the fixes

**Eight reviewers read the diff.** Everything here was introduced or exposed by the fix wave itself, not
by the survey - which is the argument for the pass existing.

| What the pass found | Status now | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **`isWashedAway`'s widening destroyed placed blocks with no drop.** Three consumers reached it through `isReplaceable`, so once the predicate covered rails, carpets, redstone and snow, fire-lighting, seed sowing and nether-wart planting could all write over them silently | **FIXED.** The two sets are decoupled on purpose: `isReplaceable` is its own list, `cellIsFree` is `isReplaceable && !isFluid`, and hoe/shovel tilling requires plain `Air`. Three asserts pin the decoupling | `Block.hpp:6746-6769`, `Main.cpp:3191-3226` |
| **Two features built with zero callers** - `takeFizzes` and `blastFuse` | **FIXED.** `takeFizzes` is drained unconditionally at `Main.cpp:7777-7780` (a gated drain would turn `recordFizz` into a permanent no-op, because the channel is capped); `blastFuse` is called per charge at `Main.cpp:8270`, deliberately drawing per charge so a chain does not give every charge the same fuse | `Main.cpp:7763-7780`, `:8240-8273` |
| **`Fluid.hpp`'s flow fix was inert** - an `isSolid` -> `isReplaceable` swap where both predicates agreed on exactly the set the bug was about, so the change compiled, read plausibly, and moved nothing | **FIXED in `Fluid.hpp`, still open in `World.cpp`.** `fluidMayOccupy` really is a different set and is asserted from both sides. But the three `World.cpp` call sites the comment names are still longhand duplicates, and one of them is a live bug - see §E.2 | `Fluid.hpp:293-325, :373` |
| **A minimise-mid-resize crash.** `freeRetiredMeshes` ran before the minimised early-return and was gated on a frame index that keeps advancing while nothing is submitted and no fence is re-checked, while chunk streaming kept retiring buffers into a command buffer that was never flushed | **FIXED.** Uploads are drained every minimised iteration and the device is waited once on entry; the same drain guards the out-of-date acquire path, which covers a window being dragged; `recreateSwapchain` returns early on a zero framebuffer and `Swapchain::create` throws rather than building a 0x0 swapchain | `Renderer.cpp:2465-2472, :2557, :1435-1453`; `Swapchain.cpp:107-113`; `Renderer.hpp:717` |
| **Undefined behaviour in a new `std::sort`** | **CHECKED AND FOUND SOUND.** Exactly one sort was added: `Renderer.cpp:2065-2068`, `std::pair<float, uint32_t>` compared with `a > b`. The float key is NaN-guarded immediately above and the second element is a unique slot index, so the comparator is a strict *total* order. Recorded here because "checked and clean" is worth as much as a fix | `Renderer.cpp:2056-2068` |
| **Coal became 42% scarcer.** The `veinHeight` triangle moved coal's mode back to `peakY` and put more of it under rock | **FIXED.** Coal's attempt count was raised 70 -> 99 to hold the realised total where tuning had already put it, and the number is now *measured* rather than asserted - 283 blocks per column, counted on both sides of the change | `TerrainGenerator.cpp:307-311, :321` |
| **Creatures were given a damage window whose comments described it as a de-duplication**, which is why it passed every reviewer assigned to it: a behaviour change was read as a refactor | **FIXED - the comments were corrected, not the code.** The code is a real 0.5 s invulnerability window and always was. The current text says so four times, explicitly: *"So this is not a de-duplication"* and *"The behavioural consequence is real and it is not a refactor"* | `Creature.cpp:788-800`; `Survival.hpp:47-52, :136-138` |
| **`Effects.hpp`'s absorption doc block was rewritten and became false again.** The old text said nothing grants Absorption; the new text says `absorptionPoints` has *"no runtime caller anywhere"* - and `Player.cpp:258` calls it in the same diff | **OPEN.** See §E.1, ledger row 126. The comment even warns that a stale version of itself was a trap, and then becomes one | `Effects.hpp:458-477, :337, :570` |

## D. Found and deliberately not fixed, with the reason

**This is the most useful section in the document.** Everything here was seen, understood, and left
alone. Most of it also carries a comment at the site, so the reasoning is where the next reader will be.

### D.1 Named divergences from the reference

Deliberate differences, all documented at the site with the words "named divergence" so they can be
grepped.

| Divergence | Reason |
|---|---|
| A standing sign has 8 rotations, not the reference's 16 | `Block.hpp:44` - `kSignStates` is the owning constant and the geometry is built from it |
| Button, pressure plate and sign are not sky-transparent, though door and trapdoor now are | `Block.hpp:6978-6981` - reasoned per family rather than by shape |
| Plants are washed away by fluids; the reference waterlogs several of them | `Block.hpp:6817` |
| A brewing stand has no twenty-second timer and no fuel charge | `Recipe.hpp:103-108` - "adding the timer means a block entity that ticks and saves, which is the furnace's whole machinery over again" |
| Carving a pumpkin yields 1 seed, not 4 | `Main.cpp:7057-7072` - Bedrock is the reference and Bedrock gives 1. The 2026-08-17 finding cited Java. The comment says "do not 'correct' this to 4" |
| Emerald generates in every biome | `TerrainGenerator.cpp:303-305` - the reference restricts it to mountains; we have no per-biome ore filter and adding one is a table change |
| Rails lay straight track only | `Main.cpp:7398-7401` |
| Thunder is delayed by distance, which the reference does not do | `Main.cpp:8667-8670` |
| A disc left in a jukebox is not saved and comes back to you on reload | `Main.cpp:2565-2567` - the block-entity file has no room for it |
| A music disc sounds one note rather than a track | `Main.cpp:5895-5898` |
| Shears and swords are 15x on their own families; several tool tiers differ | `Mining.hpp:121, :1062, :1079, :1705` |
| A turtle's scute has nowhere to go and drops anyway | `Creature.cpp:6464` |
| One hostile carries a stone sword where the reference gives gold; one creature does not drown | `Creature.cpp:1353, :1464` |
| Blast furnace input is an explicit list; smoker input is derived from `isFood` | `Furnace.cpp:22-25` - there is no smelt rule for tools or armour, so there is nothing to add for those yet |
| A container screen does not close when you walk away from the block | No range check exists. Not a duplication risk - the state stays consistent - but a divergence |

### D.2 Blocked on a feature that does not exist

| Item | Blocked on |
|---|---|
| `SoundEvent::LevelUp` - staged, decoded, no call site | There is no experience system. `BlockDrops.hpp` and `Recipe.hpp` both say so where they would otherwise award it (`Sounds.cpp:228-234`) |

### D.3 Documented rather than fixed

| Item | Why it was left |
|---|---|
| **Orphaned block entities across a format bump can duplicate items.** `chests.dat` is keyed by position and versioned separately from `kChunkFormatVersion`, which is now 6 | Two of the three holes were closed in `Main.cpp` (placement clears the cell first; the save path drops any entry whose block is no longer a container, once the column is resident). The third - a regenerated loot chest standing over a stale entry, where `materialise` finds the old contents and rolls fresh loot on top - is **live and marked WONTFIX** on the standing ruling that nothing in a save is precious. `WorldStore.cpp:198-203`, `Main.cpp:2957-2965` |
| Saves survive a full disk and a crash, but not a power cut | Only `FlushFileBuffers` would do that, "so it is knowingly not done here" (`WorldStore.cpp:509-512`) |
| The `ItemStack` padding hole is blanked at every write rather than removed | The real cure is one edit in `Item.hpp`, "which is why it has not been done in passing" (`WorldStore.hpp:174-178`) |
| `AudioEngine::load` pushes without the mutex that `play` takes | Traced: every caller is main-thread, and `unique_ptr` indirection means a reallocation moves pointers rather than `Sound`s. The intent is now written down (`AudioEngine.cpp:248-256`) |
| `kBoltTop` is a second copy of `clouds.glsl`'s cloud floor | "There is no way to assert it" - two owners, permanently (`Weather.hpp:286-288`) |
| A village chest's air guard is provably inert today | Kept, because "the chest quietly did not appear" is exactly the failure a build and a soak have nothing to say about (`Village.cpp:1621`) |
| MSVC's C4062 - the switch-coverage warning that would catch a missing enumerator - is off by default even at `/W4` and this build does not enable it | Measured, not assumed. A runtime `sweep()` and `static_assert`s substitute (`Sounds.cpp:119-124`, `Window.hpp:88-95`) |
| `strippedFor` still has a `default:` returning a real value | Acknowledged at `Block.hpp:6849-6855` as the project's third recorded failure shape; safe only because the one caller compares the result against the input |

### D.4 Measured, and judged not worth it

- **The mesher's six per-face index ranges are built and read by nobody, on purpose.** The reordering
  they exist for was measured at 1.55 ms GPU against an 8.33 ms frame - 18.6%, and the frame is
  CPU-bound. `ChunkMesher.hpp:139-152` says so and tells the reader not to "fix" the renderer to consume
  them; `ChunkMesher.cpp:269-273` keeps an assert as the only guard a dead API can have.
- **`collision::kUnstickStep` was not made finer**, although the finding that proposed it is sound. The
  constant is now shared between the player and creatures, creature heights are runtime data, and
  halving it would change which creatures are rescued from inside solid rock - moving the practical
  boundary of a suffocation clock written the same day. Left open rather than changed blind (§E.1,
  ledger row 124).

## E. Still open

> **⚠️ Re-measured 2026-08-19 by `vd-docs2`, and this section rots in the opposite direction to `GAPS.md`.**
> **Six entries were checked against source. Four were already closed; two were confirmed still live.**
> Closed: #126 (the `Effects.hpp` absorption paragraph), #127 (the HUD absorption row — 31 mentions in
> `StatusBars.*`), `fluidFeedsSideways`, and the `Block.hpp:8832` comment. Still live and re-confirmed:
> **armour durability rows** (`Mining.hpp` states it in its own words — *"A full diamond set is therefore
> permanent free protection today"*) and **`VoidPearl` has zero producers**.
>
> **Why this section is more dangerous than a stale `GAPS.md` entry, not less.** `GAPS.md` says *absent*
> about things that are *present*, and the cost is a feature built twice. **This document says *broken*
> about things that are *fixed*, and the cost is an agent editing working code** — the likely outcome is
> not a wasted hour but a regression. **`fluidFeedsSideways` was the worst possible shape**: it described
> a symptom *and wrote out the exact repair*, and the repair was already in the tree. A reader trusting it
> would have "applied" a fix that was there and had to invent a way to make the edit visible.
>
> **A stale entry here also defends itself.** The symptom description is plausible, the reader goes to code
> they do not fully understand, and they believe the document over their own reading. **So check the claim
> in source before acting on any row below** — and prefer the bare symbol name over the cited line, because
> four of the six citations checked had also moved.

## G. What the acceptance bar proves, and what it does not

**What was run, and what each thing actually establishes.**

| Check | Result | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| Both presets, `/W4` | clean, zero warnings | The program compiles. It says nothing about a table's contents |
| `tools\check-models.ps1` | 2629 / 0 | Every block that has a reference model agrees with it, box for box, and 95 of its face rectangles agree with the `uv` the reference states - **still never a pixel, only rects and extents**. It read 1792/0 while comparing union extents alone, then 2539/**275** once it also counted boxes and read `uv`s; the 275 was the tool improving, not the geometry regressing |
| `tools\check-ui-data.ps1` | clean | The UI JSON is internally consistent |
| `tools\check-index.ps1` | 704 / 0 | Every generated document index points where it says |
| `tools\check-encoding.ps1` | clean | No BOM, no U+FFFD |
| 626 `static_assert`s | pass by construction | **Table totality, permanently and for free.** Every block id has a name, a texture layer, a mining row and a drop row; no two recipes share a grid; every record on disk is the size it says |

**What none of it proves.** Nothing here observes the game. No screen was opened, no item was thrown on
the floor, no save was reloaded, no creature was watched falling. The project's own record is that three
of four faults in one milestone and both faults in another were found by **playing**, not by review, and
none of them produced a warning or a validation error. Every entry in §B is a claim about the source.

**The two shapes this round is most likely to have introduced, given the recurring list:** a widened
predicate that killed an early-out behind it (the `isWashedAway` regression in §C was exactly this, and
it was found by a reviewer rather than by the compiler), and a derivation applied to one of a pair and
not the other (`fluidFeedsSideways` in §E.2 is exactly this, and it is still live).

## 0. How this was produced, and what it is worth

> **HISTORY - the method note for the 2026-08-17 audit.** The 2026-08-18 round used a different method - 21 exclusive areas, a findings ledger, 16 fix agents batched by owning file, then 8 verification reviewers - described in **§A**. The warning here about static review applies to both rounds and has not weakened.

**Method: static review only.** The machine was under load, so the developer's instruction was explicit —
no builds, no `run.ps1`, no `tools\soak.ps1`, nothing that launches `game.exe`. Everything below was found
by *reading the code and reasoning about it*, which has one important consequence:

> **This audit could not confirm any fault by watching it happen.** Each finding carries a confidence
> rating instead — `certain` means the code was read and it is wrong, `likely` means the code is wrong but
> whether a player reaches it is unproven, and `worth checking` means it smells and has not been disproved.
> Treat `certain` as work to schedule and `worth checking` as a question, not a bug.

Five independent reviewers were run in parallel over separate areas, each given the project's own list of
recurring bug shapes from `CLAUDE.md` as a hunting brief, plus direct measurement of the repository.
**Their reports are reproduced verbatim in §4 onward** — nothing summarised away, because a paraphrased
`file:line` is worth nothing when you sit down to fix it.

**What was NOT reviewed** is listed honestly in §9. It is not a small list.

---

## 1. The headline, in plain English

> **HISTORY - superseded by §A.** Written before the 2026-08-18 round. Its "no autosave" headline is closed (**§B.3**); its art paragraphs are retired by the developer's ruling, not fixed.

**The engineering is finished and the product is not.**

That is the whole state of the project in one sentence. Milestones 1–29 are done and the game is genuinely,
substantially built — a real endless world, survival, farming, villages, 57 creature species, a modern
renderer with shadows and weather and reflections, and 2,871 blocks. What is left on the route is three
*experimental* milestones (ray tracing, advanced simulation, global illumination), one *optional* one
(developer tooling), and only **two marked Core: settings (M34) and packaging (M35)**.

Both of those are shipping work, not features. Which means:

> **The project has run out of "build the game" and has not yet started "turn it into a product."**
> The gap between those two is much larger than it looks, and almost none of it is code.

Three things sit in that gap, and only one of them is on the route at all:

1. **The art.** Every texture, creature skin, sprite, font glyph and sound recording currently in front of
   the player is Mojang's, staged from a 662 MB folder that is deliberately gitignored and can never ship.
   **987 textures, 53 skins, 57 sprites, a font, a HUD sheet and 497 sound recordings still have to be
   authored**, and the job **does not appear as a milestone** — it is a cross-cutting "track" delegated to a
   friend with no deadline. §3 and §14.1 measure it.
2. **The bugs the acceptance bar cannot see.** The project's own documentation already says this plainly
   ("both presets clean proves it does not crash and almost nothing else"). This audit confirms it again:
   five reviewers found real, confirmed faults in code that has passed that bar many times — including
   **silent item destruction**, **a save-path that can permanently install broken geometry**, and, worst of
   all, **no autosave at all**, so any crash costs the whole session's inventory, chests and creatures while
   *keeping* the terrain those things stood in.
3. **Packaging and settings.** Real, bounded, and genuinely the smallest of the three — but note that
   packaging today would **redistribute Mojang's textures, font and sounds**, because the game prefers the
   reference art staged beside the executable and there is no packaging step that excludes it (§11.5).

**Is the project in good shape?** Yes — better than most solo engine projects ever get, and the
discipline behind it (§8) is unusually strong. But the honest reading is that it is *at* the point where
ambition has to give way to finishing, and the route as written points the other way: the next milestone
listed is hardware ray tracing.

---

> `SYSTEM_MEMORY.md`, `START-HERE.md` and `CLAUDE.md` were grepped afterwards and **state no line counts at
> all**, so there is no stale number in them to fix. The advice attached to that observation is still good
> and is kept in §11.

| Total lines of source | **62,036** (55,982 excluding blank lines) |

| Next largest | `Creature.cpp` 7,887 · `Main.cpp` 7,108 · `Renderer.cpp` 2,383 · `Item.hpp` 2,149 · `World.cpp` 2,079 |
| **Largest single function** | **`main()` — 6,131 lines** (`Main.cpp:978` to end of file) |
| `static_assert` uses | **234** |

**Three of these are findings in their own right** and are picked up later: the 6,131-line `main()` (§7.1),
the uncompressed chunk format (§6, B-New-1), and the single `std::atomic` against 26 mutex uses (§8).

**Verified clean, so nobody need spend the time again:**

- **`engine/` does not know `game/` exists.** Grepped the entire engine tree for any include or reference to
  game concepts (blocks, chunks, player, creature) — **zero violations**. The architecture rule that most
  projects quietly break is genuinely being held.
- **Every documentation index is accurate.** 617 entries checked, 0 wrong. Every one of the 13 documents
  reports "up to date".
- **No encoding rot.** No BOM, no U+FFFD, no mojibake across all markdown (the 5 hits in `LESSONS.md` are
  the lessons quoting the detector, which is expected).
- **The working tree is clean** and nothing has been committed unprompted.

## 3. The art problem, measured

> **RETIRED, not fixed.** The repository is private and Mojang's assets stay permanently. Kept for the reasoning only. **Do not act on it.**

This is the biggest single item in the project and it is worth stating numerically, because the prose
description ("most creature skins are placeholders") badly understates it.

> **Corrected after the strategy review (§14.1), which measured the loader rather than the first texture
> list.** My original figure — "68 named layers, 38 ours, 30 Mojang's" — describes only the *first* texture
> array. The `kExtraBlocks` runs add roughly a thousand more names. **The real number is 987 textures still
> to be authored.** The table below is the corrected one.

| Thing | Ours | Still to author |
|---|---|---|
| Distinct named PNG textures requested by `Main.cpp` | **110** of 1,097 | **987** |
| Creature skins | 4 | **53** |
| Spawn-egg sprites | 0 | **57** |
| Catalogue tab icons | 0 | **5** |
| Font sheet | placeholder | **1** |
| HUD sheet | **Mojang's, and it ships** — see §14.7b | **1** |
| Sound recordings | 0 | **497** (plus 34 voice families, 8 music tracks) |

Staged beside the executable today: **1,354 reference PNGs and 519 sound files.** That folder *is* the
shippable artifact.

**What this means in plain English:** if the `reference/` folder were deleted tomorrow, the game would still
run — the loader falls back to our own art, then to a blank white square, and logs every name it could not
find (`Main.cpp:1017-1032`). It would just be a game of white cubes in silence. **That fallback is good
engineering and it is also what hides the size of the problem.**

**And there is a sharper point.** The reference art wins *unconditionally* — every loader checks the staged
reference first and there is no setting to flip it. So **not even the 110 textures we own are on screen**,
and nobody involved in this project has ever seen the game that can actually ship. Every visual decision
from M23 onward — tone map, exposure, bloom, fog, water colour, the whole of Phase 6 — was tuned against
Mojang's palette.

**This is sanctioned and deliberate** — the developer's documentation is emphatic that development runs on
reference art on purpose and that an agent must not hand-author replacements. So it is not a mistake. It is
an **unscheduled dependency on one other person**, sitting in front of the only two Core milestones left,
with roughly a third of it (332 colour- and wood-family variants) being mechanical work an agent could do
today with the generator that already exists.

**One premise of mine was wrong, and it is good news:** `tools/check-models.ps1` compares *box extents* from
the reference's model JSON and never looks at a pixel, so **replacing the art does not threaten it**. What
*does* couple to art is the creature UV nets — if a skin is authored in a different layout, every mob
mistextures and nothing but the human eye will catch it. §14.2 has the detail.

## 4. Findings — gameplay, inventory and items

> **CLOSED.** All eight findings were fixed across 2026-08-17 and 2026-08-18; carrying `damage` and answering "will these items fit" now have single owners with compile-time proofs. See **§B.1**. Every `file:line` below is stale by hundreds of lines.

> Reproduced verbatim from the reviewer that covered `Main.cpp`, `SlotOps.cpp`, `Block.hpp`, `Inventory`,
> `InventoryScreen`, `WorldStore` chunk I/O and coordinate maths.

### 4.1 `damage` is dropped on every "hand the item back / throw it away" path — stowbox contents destroyed, damaged tools free-repaired
**`game/src/Main.cpp:2794`, `2796`, `3234`, `3775`, `4478`** · confidence: **certain**

A player Q-drops a stowbox (or closes the inventory with one on the cursor) and its 27 stored items are gone forever; Q-dropping a nearly-broken pickaxe and picking it up returns it at full durability.

`ItemEntity.hpp:29-34` states the contract outright — *"`damage` rides along untouched. It is a tool's wear for most items, and **which stored contents a stowbox is** for those — either way, dropping something and picking it up again must not change it."* The pickup side honours it (`Main.cpp:6158`: `inventory.add(ready.item, ready.count, ready.damage)`), and the break-a-chest spill honours it (`Main.cpp:4686-4687`: `drops.spawn(centre, stack.item, stack.count, glm::vec3{0.0f}, 0.35f, stack.damage)`). The outbound paths do not:

```cpp
// Main.cpp:2789  closeScreen / giveBack
const int left = inventory.add(stack.item, stack.count);            // damage defaults to 0
if (left > 0) {
    drops.spawn(camera.position + camera.forward() * 0.5f, stack.item, left,
                camera.forward() * kThrowSpeed, kThrowPickupDelay); // damage defaults to 0
}
```
```cpp
// Main.cpp:3234  Q with a screen open
drops.spawn(camera.position + camera.forward() * 0.5f, heldStack.item, heldStack.count,
            camera.forward() * kThrowSpeed, kThrowPickupDelay);
// Main.cpp:3775  left/right click outside the panel
drops.spawn(camera.position + camera.forward() * 0.5f, heldStack.item, thrown,
            camera.forward() * kThrowSpeed, kThrowPickupDelay);
// Main.cpp:4478  Q from the hotbar, no screen open
drops.spawn(camera.position + camera.forward() * 0.5f, held.item, 1,
            camera.forward() * kThrowSpeed, kThrowPickupDelay);
```
Signature `ItemEntity.hpp:33` / `Inventory.hpp:38` both default `damage = 0`, so the compiler cannot flag it. This is bug shape #9 (rule correct in one of the places that needs it) with the stowbox-in-`damage` hazard you called out.

> **Fixed 2026-08-17 — and there were eleven sites, not eight.** `game::dropStack(ItemEntities&, const glm::vec3&, const ItemStack&, ...)` was written exactly as recommended and every path above now calls it, along with three this table did not find: the shift-click craft loop, the screen give-back, and the second furnace spill. `ItemEntities::spawn`'s defaulted `damage` parameter is no longer reachable from any of them. Verified by reading the call sites and by a clean `/W4` build; **no one has thrown a stowbox on the floor and picked it up again.**

### 4.2 `slots::rightClick` rebuilds the cursor stack without `damage` — split/take destroys stowbox contents and repairs tools
**`game/src/item/SlotOps.cpp:52`** · confidence: **certain**

Right-clicking a stowbox in any slot picks it up as an *empty* stowbox; right-clicking a damaged tool picks it up at full durability.

```cpp
const int taken = (slot.count + 1) / 2;
cursor = ItemStack{slot.item, taken};   // <-- slot.damage is never copied
slot.count -= taken;
```
`ItemStack` is `{item, count, damage}` (`Item.hpp`), so the two-arg braced init zeroes `damage`. Because `maxStackFor` a stowbox and a tool is 1 (`Item.hpp:1979-1981`, `1551-1554`), `taken == 1` and the whole stack moves — so this is not an edge case, it is *every* right-click on a tool or stowbox. `merge()` two functions above does copy it (`to.damage = from.damage`, line 20), which is why this reads as an oversight rather than a decision.

> **Fixed 2026-08-17.** The rebuilt cursor stack carries `damage` across. This was the widest of the three `damage` faults by frequency — a right-click is the most ordinary click in the game — and it is now also covered from the other side, because `slots::roomFor` answers zero for anything that cannot stack, so two damaged items can no longer be merged at all.

### 4.3 Explosion cleanup handles only `isChest`, not hoppers or lecterns — contents lost, stale entry left keyed at the cell
**`game/src/Main.cpp:6309-6318`** · confidence: **likely**

TNT a hopper: its five items vanish (nothing spills), and if the player later places any container on that exact block, the old contents reappear inside it.

The break path is explicit about the three:
```cpp
// Main.cpp:4670
if (game::isChest(broken) || game::isHopper(broken) ||
    broken == game::BlockId::Lectern) {
```
The blast path is not:
```cpp
// Main.cpp:6309
if (game::isChest(removed)) {
    const auto found = chests.find(cell);
    ...
    chests.erase(found);
}
```
So `chests` keeps a live entry at a cell that is now Air. `Main.cpp:5818` (`chests[where] = ...`) and `Main.cpp:3542` (`chests.find(where)`) both key purely on position, so a newly placed container inherits it. Bug shape #9 again.

> **Fixed 2026-08-17.** `Main.cpp:6641` now asks `isChest(removed) || isHopper(removed) || removed == BlockId::Lectern`, matching the break path, and erases the `chests` entry in every case, so the stale-entry inheritance is gone too. Two things were fixed alongside it that this finding did not ask for: a blown-up **stowbox keeps its contents**, which are moved onto the dropped item under a fresh handle rather than scattered (the reference's rule, and §11.2 #6), and a screen still open on the destroyed block is closed, because it was showing a copy of contents that had already dropped.

### 4.4 Second half of a double chest spills without `damage`
**`game/src/Main.cpp:4713`** · confidence: **certain**

Break the left half of a double chest that had a full stowbox in the *right* half → the stowbox pops out empty.

Twenty-seven lines apart, in the same `if` block, the two spills disagree:
```cpp
// Main.cpp:4686 — first half, correct
drops.spawn(centre, stack.item, stack.count, glm::vec3{0.0f}, 0.35f, stack.damage);
// Main.cpp:4713 — partner half, damage lost
drops.spawn(centre, stack.item, stack.count);
```
The same omission is at `Main.cpp:4658` and `6303` (furnace slots) and `6315` (blasted chest). #4658/#6303 are low impact (furnace slots hold no damaged items in practice); 4713 and 6315 are not.

> **Fixed 2026-08-17** by the same `dropStack` change as §4.1 — both halves now go through one function, which is the point of it.

### 4.5 `Inventory::hasRoomFor` and `slots::quickMove` / `gather` match on `item` alone, ignoring `damage`
**`game/src/item/Inventory.cpp:41-52`, `game/src/item/SlotOps.cpp:100-112`, `126-130`** · confidence: **worth checking**

Shift-clicking or double-click-gathering things whose `damage` is data could merge two distinct objects into one.

```cpp
// SlotOps.cpp:104
if (target->empty() || target->item != from.item) { continue; }   // damage not compared
merge(*target, from, from.count);                                  // to.damage = from.damage
```
`Inventory::add` (`Inventory.cpp:19`) *does* compare `stack.damage == damage`. Today the two stowboxes/tools are saved by `maxStackFor == 1` making `room == 0` in `merge` (`SlotOps.cpp:14-16`), so no loss occurs — I verified this, so it is not currently exploitable. But `hasRoomFor` (`Inventory.cpp:47`) still counts a mismatched-damage stack as room, which can make the shift-click craft loop at `Main.cpp:3796` think it has space it does not. Flagging because the invariant is enforced nowhere and the `static_assert` at `Item.hpp:1979` is the only thing holding it up.

> **Fixed 2026-08-17, by giving the question one owner rather than patching three answers.** `constexpr slots::roomFor(const ItemStack& dest, const ItemStack& src)` is now the only place that decides whether a stack may accept items, and `Inventory::add`, `hasRoomFor`, `quickMove`, `gather` and `distribute` all count with it. It returns zero for anything whose max stack is one, which closes this finding and §11.2 #4 in the same line. Both sides are `constexpr`, so the `static_assert`s beside it can never rot.

### 4.6 `inventoryScreen::craftSize` has a `default:` returning a real grid size
**`game/src/hud/InventoryScreen.hpp:66-79`** · confidence: **worth checking** (latent, exactly bug shape #6)

A new screen kind added later silently gets a 2×2 crafting grid and four unreachable-but-writable slots.

```cpp
    case Kind::Stonecutter:
        return 0;
    default:
        return 2;          // only Kind::Inventory reaches here today
    }
```
Every other kind is listed explicitly; only `Inventory` relies on the default. Because `craftSlotCount` feeds the `craftSlots` array and `closeScreen`'s give-back loop, a missing entry becomes an item-handling bug, not a compile error. Naming `Kind::Inventory` and deleting the `default:` would let `-Wswitch` do the work.

### 4.7 `blockFacing` early-outs on `isFurnace` before the six-way machine cases
**`game/src/world/Block.hpp:7493`** · confidence: **worth checking**

Verified **not** currently broken, but it is the exact shape you asked about. `isFurnace` (`Block.hpp:2715-2718`) was widened to `|| isSmoker(id) || isBlastFurnace(id)`, and it is the *first* test in `blockFacing`. Worth a comment there so the next widening does not break it.

### 4.8 Chunk size is stated twice, in two files, in two forms
**`game/src/world/Creature.cpp:566-568`** vs **`game/src/world/Chunk.hpp:18`** · confidence: **worth checking** (bug shape #1, currently benign)

```cpp
// Creature.cpp
/// Chunks are 32 blocks, so a coordinate shifts by five.

```
`Chunk::kSize = 32` owns this. The shift is then used for real coordinate maths (`Creature.cpp:4565-4566`, `4581-4582`). I confirmed 1<<5 == 32 today, so **this is not a live bug**. But the spawner is the one place that does `>> kChunkShift` instead of `floorDiv(x, Chunk::kSize)`, and if `Chunk::kSize` ever moves the spawner silently keeps the old grid. (Everything else — `World.cpp:20-30` `floorDiv`/`floorMod`, `TerrainGenerator.hpp:22` `floorDivInt`, `Main.cpp:690-714`, `Structures.cpp:529-532`, `Village.cpp:1339-1342` — uses floor division correctly on negative coordinates; I checked every `%`/`/` hit and found no truncation-toward-zero fault.)

### 4.9 Verified correct — do not re-spend time here

- **Water vs lava pooling** (`World.cpp:869-877` `fluidFeedsSideways` vs `World.cpp:1182-1186`): the "a cell resting on more fluid is partway down a column" clause is present in **both**, with a comment on each saying so. The historical asymmetry is fixed.
- **Stowbox handle allocation** (`Main.cpp:2624-2628`): `nextStowHandle = std::max(nextStowHandle, box.handle + 1)` after load — no collision with handles restored from `stowboxes.dat`.
- **Double-chest slot resolution** (`Main.cpp:3540-3545`, `3583-3597`): `at.index < kChestSlots ? openChestPosition : openChestPartner` plus `at.index % kChestSlots` is correct for 0..53; the `shown` cap correctly restricts a hopper to 5.
- **Drop pickup** (`Main.cpp:6158-6165`): partial pickup and `damage` are both handled; `break` after `reduce` avoids index invalidation.
- **Chunk save/load** (`WorldStore.cpp:150-195`): every header field is validated, version mismatch returns `nullopt` silently, waterlogged bits are appended so an old file degrades correctly.
- **Potion durations** (`Item.hpp:455-483`): seconds, not ticks — Slowness IV at 20 s and Poison II at 22.5 s match the reference. Projectile `power`/`gravity` stay in blocks-per-tick end to end (`Projectile.hpp:51-53`, `Main.cpp:4508-4511`, `5285-5286`), so no unit mixing there.

**Reviewer's suggested fix order:** 4.2 and 4.1 first (one-line each, and they are the same root cause reachable from five different player actions), then 4.4, then 4.3.

## 5. Findings — renderer, GPU and threading

> **CLOSED, with two later additions.** 5.1's minimise path was fixed *again* on 2026-08-18, after a verification reviewer found a retire-while-minimised use-after-free the first fix did not cover (**§C**); 5.5's single-buffered attachments were re-examined and confirmed safe. See **§B.8**.

> Reproduced verbatim from the reviewer that covered `Renderer.cpp`, `UploadContext.cpp`, `World.cpp`'s job
> dispatch, `JobSystem.cpp` and the architecture rules.

### 5.1 Retired GPU buffers can be freed while the GPU still reads them — the minimise path bypasses every fence
`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:2229-2241` · confidence: **certain** (logic), **likely** (observable)

```cpp
// Before any early return, so a minimized or resizing window still releases
// retired buffers instead of accumulating them.
++m_frameIndex;
freeRetiredMeshes();

if (m_window.isMinimized()) {
    return;
}
...
vkCheck(vkWaitForFences(device, 1, &m_frameInFlight[m_currentFrame], ...
```
`freeRetiredMeshes` (`Renderer.cpp:1046-1059`) frees on a **CPU frame counter**, not on a fence:
```cpp
constexpr std::uint64_t framesToHold = kFramesInFlight + 1;
const auto expired = [&](const RetiredMesh& r) { return m_frameIndex - r.retiredOnFrame >= framesToHold; };
```
The invariant "frame N is complete by the time `m_frameIndex == N+3`" holds **only because each non-minimised `drawFrame` waits on `m_frameInFlight[m_currentFrame]`**. Minimised iterations increment `m_frameIndex` and free, but never wait, and never submit.

Interleaving: `drawFrame(N)` submits a command buffer binding buffer B → game calls `updateMesh`/`removeMesh`, `retire(B)` with `retiredOnFrame = N` (`Renderer.cpp:1031-1038`) → user minimises → iterations N+1, N+2, N+3 each run `++m_frameIndex; freeRetiredMeshes(); return;` in microseconds → at N+3 `vkDestroyBuffer`/`vkFreeMemory` runs on B while frame N's submission is still executing on the queue. Same hole applies to `m_currentFrame` never advancing while minimised, so the slot's fence is never re-checked.

Fix shape: hold retired buffers keyed to a *completed-fence* index, or `return` before `++m_frameIndex`, or `vkDeviceWaitIdle` once on entering the minimised state.

### 5.2 A chunk unload/reload resets `revision` to 0 and lets a stale in-flight mesh install permanently
`game/src/world/World.cpp:1847` (collection) and `World.cpp:1953-1963` (upload) · confidence: **certain**

```cpp
m_chunks.emplace(result.coord, ChunkSlot{std::move(result.blocks), false, false, false, false, 0});
```
```cpp
if (it->second.revision != result.revision) { queueMesh(result.coord); continue; }
```
The revision guard described at `World.hpp:283-287` ("a result whose revision no longer matches is thrown away") is defeated because the counter restarts at 0 for a re-emplaced chunk.

Interleaving: chunk C loaded, `revision == 0`; `dispatchMeshes` copies its volume and submits job J with `revision = 0` (`World.cpp:1806-1813`) → player edits nothing, walks past `m_unloadRadius`; C is erased (`World.cpp:1889-1906`) while J is still running and C stays in `m_meshInFlight` → player walks back; C is re-generated/loaded and emplaced with `revision = 0`, `meshed = false` → J lands, `collectFinishedJobs` erases C from `m_meshInFlight` and pushes the result → upload loop finds `revision 0 == 0` and sets `meshed = true`, `detailBuilt` from J's tier.

Two distinct consequences: (a) if the chunk was edited during its *first* residency and the edit bumped it to rev 1, then the *rev-0* job that was still in flight from before the edit now matches the reloaded slot's rev 0, so pre-edit geometry is installed and, because `slot.meshed == true` and `detailBuilt == detailWanted`, `refreshQueues` (`World.cpp:1698-1706`) will never pick it up again — a permanent stale mesh; (b) the mesh is built at the *old* tier, so a chunk can be stuck terrain-only inside the detail radius. `m_meshInFlight` is likewise not cleared when a chunk is unloaded, so between the unload and J's collection a fresh `dispatchMeshes` for the reloaded C is silently dropped by `if (m_meshInFlight.count(coord) != 0) continue;` (`World.cpp:1789-1791`).

Fix shape: never reset `revision` on re-emplacement (keep a monotonic per-coord counter, or seed it from a generation stamp), and drop `m_meshInFlight`/`m_loadInFlight` entries for coords that unload.

> **Fixed 2026-08-17.** The counter is now `World::m_nextRevision`, monotonic for the life of the session and living **outside** the chunk slot, so an unload/reload cannot reset it. A result carrying a revision older than the chunk's current one is discarded rather than installed. This was the one renderer-side fault in today's session; §5.1, §5.3, §5.4 and §5.5 are untouched.

### 5.3 Every blended draw in the forward pass writes depth
`engine/src/render/Renderer.cpp:203-212` · confidence: **certain** (the state) / **likely** (the artefact)

> **Corrected 2026-08-17, later the same day.** The half of this finding about the **HUD is wrong and is
> retracted.** The UI is not drawn through the world pipeline at all: `recordUiPass`
> (`Renderer.cpp:2128-2149`) runs *after* tone mapping, straight into the swapchain, and its
> `VkRenderingInfo` has **no depth attachment whatsoever** — the code says so in as many words, *"No depth
> attachment. That is the whole point of this pass."* UI ordering is instead handled on the CPU: each of
> the three screen meshes (main, clipped, top) is sorted back-to-front by maximum z before upload
> (`Renderer.cpp:144-172`). So `Renderer.hpp`'s prose about "ordering is the only fix while the HUD shares
> the world pipeline" describes a state of affairs that no longer exists.
>
> **What survives, and it is the important half:** the *water and translucent world geometry* case below
> is unaffected, because the forward pass genuinely does have a depth attachment. Read the rest of this
> finding as being about water, particles and the crack mesh only. See `UI.md` §1 for the real UI path.

`m_trianglePipeline` supplies **no** `depthTest`/`depthWrite`/`blend`, so it takes the `PipelineDesc` defaults at `GraphicsPipeline.hpp:48-50`: `depthTest = true`, `depthWrite = true`, `blend = BlendMode::Alpha`.
```cpp
m_trianglePipeline = std::make_unique<GraphicsPipeline>(
    context.device(), PipelineDesc{
                          .vertexSpirv = ... "triangle.vert.spv",
                          .fragmentSpirv = ... "triangle.frag.spv",
                          .colorFormats = {kSceneColorFormat},
                          .depthFormat = m_depthImage->format(),
                          .descriptorSetLayout = m_descriptorSetLayout,
                          .pushConstantBytes = sizeof(MeshPushConstants),
                      });
```
The clouds (`:283-284`) and precipitation (`:301-302`) pipelines each explicitly say `depthWrite = false` with the comment *"a blended fragment that stamps its distance punches a rectangular hole through everything drawn after it"* — the world/HUD pipeline is the one that never got the same treatment. `Renderer.hpp:120-128` admits it in prose: *"a blended fragment still writes depth… That is exactly what the stack on the cursor did to the catalogue behind it. Ordering is the only fix while the HUD shares the world pipeline."*

What this reaches, all through `drawMesh` at `Renderer.cpp:1848-1866`: translucent chunk meshes (water) at `:1902-1913`, the overlay/held item `:1915`, the crack mesh `:1921`, the particle mesh `:1926`, the lightning bolt `:1930`. The water case is the live one: the translucent loop iterates `m_meshes` in **slot order**, not sorted back-to-front, so with depth-write on, a nearer water chunk drawn first depth-rejects the farther one — visible seams/holes across chunk borders in a lake, which vary as slots are recycled by streaming. Note the code *relies* on water writing depth for rain rejection (`:1926-1932` comment), so this is a genuine design conflict, not a one-line flip.

### 5.4 `recreateSwapchain` destroys semaphores that a pending present may still wait on
`Renderer.cpp:1358-1376` · confidence: **worth checking**

Calls `vkDeviceWaitIdle` then `destroySyncObjects(); createSyncObjects();`. `vkDeviceWaitIdle` drains queue *execution*, but a `vkQueuePresentKHR` already issued against `m_renderFinished[imageIndex]` (`Renderer.cpp:2367-2374`) is a presentation-engine operation; the spec does not let you destroy a semaphore with a pending wait on this basis alone. Trigger: present returns `VK_SUBOPTIMAL_KHR`/resize flag → immediate `recreateSwapchain()` on the very next statement. Validation layers would flag this; a soak test would not. Everything else about the resize path checked out — depth image, all render targets, and `writePostDescriptorSets` are rebuilt (`Renderer.hpp:407-411`, `Renderer.cpp:1360-1366`), `m_currentFrame` reset, `m_timestampsPending` cleared.

### 5.5 Every offscreen attachment is single-buffered across 2 frames in flight
`Renderer.hpp:601-606` · confidence: **certain** (state) / benign-but-costly

`m_sceneColor`, `m_sceneCopy`, `m_bloom`, `m_gbufferAlbedo/Light/Material`, `m_depthImage` are single `unique_ptr`s, while `kFramesInFlight = 2`. This is *not* a race, because each pass re-transitions with `vkCmdPipelineBarrier` from `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED` (`Renderer.cpp:1567-1585`) and barriers order against all earlier submissions on the same queue — but it means frame N+1's geometry pass cannot overlap frame N's tone-map, so the two-frame pipeline buys almost nothing. Listed here because it is the thing most likely to be mistaken for a race; it is a perf item (see 6.B4).

What *is* correct and was verified: the frame uniform buffer and its descriptor set are per-frame (`Renderer.hpp:539-546`, `Renderer.cpp:886-889`, `971-977`), the deferred set is per-frame (`Renderer.cpp:437-439`), command buffers are per-frame (`:874-880`), and the uniform write at `Renderer.cpp:2288` happens strictly after the fence wait at `:2248` with the reasoning spelled out in-line.

### 5.6 `UploadContext` mid-batch flush is a full CPU→GPU stall inside the streaming loop
`engine/src/render/UploadContext.cpp:110-113` then `:57-88` · confidence: **certain** (perf-correctness)

```cpp
if (m_recording && m_arenaOffset + bytes > m_arenaCapacity) { flush(); }
beginRecording();          // -> recycleArena()
...
vkCheck(vkWaitForFences(m_context.device(), 1, &m_fence, VK_TRUE, UINT64_MAX), "vkWaitForFences");
```
Whenever a frame's chunk uploads exceed the 16 MB arena (`Renderer.cpp:196`), the *next* `stage()` blocks the main thread until the GPU has finished the copy submission. One arena, one fence, no double-buffering. Visible as a hitch while flying, not as corruption.

### 5.7 Architecture rules — verified clean, with caveats

- **Rule 2 (generation pure):** upheld. `World.cpp:1743-1752` captures only `coord`, `seed`, and `shared_ptr`s: `m_jobs.submit([coord, seed = m_seed, store = m_store, results = m_results] {...})`, and no globals/`Clock::now` exist in `TerrainGenerator.cpp`, `Noise.cpp`, `Structures.cpp`, `Village.cpp` (grepped for `g_`, `static` mutables, `thread_local`, `Clock::now`, `rand` — nothing).
- **Rule 3/4 (meshing pure, one owner):** upheld, and unusually well. `gatherVolume` copies the chunk plus a one-cell border **on the main thread** (`World.hpp:352-364`, `World.cpp:1795-1805`), the job owns a `shared_ptr<MeshJobInput>`, and `meshChunk` returns vertex data that the main thread uploads. No worker touches `m_chunks`. `JobResults` (`World.hpp:302-313`) is the only shared state and its mutex covers all of it; it is held by `shared_ptr` so `World::~World() = default` (`World.cpp:113`) is genuinely safe.
- **`WorldStore` is stateless** (`WorldStore.hpp:150-154`: a path and a seed, all methods `const`), so the worker-`load` / main-thread-`save` overlap is not a data race, and one-file-per-chunk + temp-rename means a same-chunk collision is impossible anyway since `dispatchLoads` skips coords already in `m_chunks`.
- **`JobSystem`** (`engine/src/core/JobSystem.cpp`) is correct on inspection: `m_outstanding` decrement is under the mutex, the destructor's `m_outstanding -= m_queue.size()` can't underflow, `threadCount == 0` runs inline.
- **Rules 1 and 6** (engine→game leakage, `Vk*` in gameplay) were left unverified by this reviewer. **They have since been checked directly and are clean** — see §2.

## 6. Optimisations worth doing

> **MOSTLY OPEN.** Only the generation cost was addressed, by a per-chunk climate cache (**§B.6**). B1-B7 are untouched and chunk files are still stored completely uncompressed. Nothing here was re-measured on 2026-08-18.

> Reproduced verbatim from the renderer reviewer, plus one new item from direct measurement.
> **Every one of these carries the measurement that must be run first.** That is the project's own
> hard-won rule: measure before optimising, and the answer will not be one of the three you would have
> guessed.

### B1. Per-chunk draw calls with a full push-constant + vertex/index rebind, twice (shadow ×cascades, then G-buffer)
**High payoff, low-medium effort.** `Renderer.cpp:1520-1543` (shadow) and `1848-1866` (forward) rebind a vertex buffer, an index buffer and push 64+ bytes **per mesh, per cascade**. Every chunk mesh owns its own `Buffer` pair (`Renderer.hpp:418-437`), so there is no way to batch. **Measure first:** `m_stats.drawCalls` is already reported (`Renderer.hpp:44-46`) — log draw calls split by pass at render distance 12+. If shadow-pass draws are ≈ `cascades × opaque chunks`, that alone justifies sub-allocating chunk meshes into a few large buffers and switching to `vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirect`. The `deviceAllocations` warning at `Renderer.cpp:2299-2306` says the author already expects this ceiling.

### B2. Shadow cascades re-draw the whole world per cascade with no per-cascade distance cap
**High payoff, low effort.** `Renderer.cpp:1523-1526` culls with `boxInFrustum(frustumPlanes(m_shadowMatrices[cascade]), ...)` and `beyondFog`, but nothing restricts cascade 0 to near geometry — a chunk inside two cascades' boxes is drawn twice. **Measure first:** count draws and triangles per cascade separately (one counter each, ~5 lines, already have `m_frameTriangles`), and compare GPU ms with `setShadowQuality(0)` (which skips the pass entirely, `Renderer.hpp:196-203`) against quality 3. If the delta is >2 ms you have your answer without guessing.

### B3. Greedy-meshing quality / interior geometry
**Potentially the largest win, but measure or you will waste the effort.** This is exactly the project's own lesson (the 65%-sealed-in-rock probe). Before touching `ChunkMesher.cpp`, re-run that probe as a triangle histogram: bin `m_frameTriangles` by whether the emitting chunk is above/below the local surface, or simply log total scene triangles vs. triangles that survive the depth test. This reviewer did **not** read `ChunkMesher.cpp`, so treat any claim that it does or does not already merge coplanar faces as unverified.

### B4. Double-buffer the G-buffer/scene targets, or accept the serialisation
**Medium payoff, medium effort — premature until measured.** See 5.5. The barriers from `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_UNDEFINED` at `Renderer.cpp:1567-1585` serialise frame N+1 against frame N. **Measure first:** compare `m_stats.gpuMilliseconds` (device timestamps, `Renderer.cpp:1401-1406`/`1447-1450`) against wall-clock frame time. If GPU ms ≈ frame ms, you are GPU-serialised and duplicating attachments helps; if GPU ms is well under frame time, you are CPU-bound and this buys nothing. On a 4070 Laptop the second is more likely, which is precisely why this must not be done on intuition.

### B5. Upload arena double-buffering
**Medium payoff, low effort.** Fixes 5.6. Two arenas + two fences, alternating, removes the mid-frame stall. **Measure first:** `UploadContext` already counts `m_submissions` (`UploadContext.cpp:145`) — expose it per frame; more than one submission per frame while flying means the arena is overflowing and the stall is real. If it is always 1, skip this.

### B6. Overdraw in the forward pass / no occlusion culling
**Low-medium payoff, high effort — premature.** Frustum culling exists (`boxInFrustum`, `beyondFog` at `Renderer.cpp:1063-1076`) but there is no occlusion query or HiZ. Given B3's precedent, the cheap measurement is a full-screen overdraw counter (render depth-only, count fragments) before writing any occlusion system.

### B7. CPU per-frame allocations: `setScreenMesh`/`setParticleMesh`/`setPrecipitationMesh` rebuild and re-upload whole meshes every frame
Each goes through `uploadInto` → `retire` + two fresh `Buffer` allocations (`Renderer.cpp:1031-1038`, `1078+`). `retiredMeshCount()` (`Renderer.hpp:389`) is the ready-made probe: **if it does not hover near zero, or if it is ~4-6 every frame, you are churning device allocations for the HUD**. Fix is a persistent per-frame-in-flight ring buffer for dynamic geometry. Low effort once measured.

### B-New-1. Chunk files are stored completely uncompressed — 68 KB every time, for a mostly-empty or mostly-solid volume
**High payoff, low effort. Not in the reviewers' reports; found by direct measurement.**

`WorldStore.cpp:211-226` writes the header, then `Chunk::kBlockBytes` raw, then the waterlogging bits. A chunk is 32³ = 32,768 cells × 2 bytes = 65,536 bytes, plus 4,096 bytes of waterlogging = **68 KB per chunk, always**, whether it is solid stone, empty air, or a village.

Measured on the current save: **82 modified chunks = 5.4 MB.** That is fine. It scales badly: a chunk only has to be *touched* to be written, and the project's own `CLAUDE.md` notes that merely standing near an ocean flags chunks modified because water flow calls `setBlock`. A world explored across even a modest area writes hundreds of megabytes.

Voxel data is the single most compressible thing in a game — the overwhelming majority of chunks are one or two block ids repeated. A **palette plus run-length encoding** typically gets 20–100× on this data and is perhaps 80 lines. **Measure first:** the honest probe is to take the current 82 chunk files and run any general-purpose compressor over them; if a plain zip of `saves/` is under 300 KB, the ceiling is real and worth taking. `kChunkFormatVersion` exists precisely to make this change safe, and it is already at 4.

## 7. Structure and process

> **OPEN, and 7.1 moved the wrong way.** `main()` is now roughly 8,000 lines from `Main.cpp:1102`. There is still no automated test suite; 626 `static_assert`s landed instead - see **§G** for what that does and does not prove.

### 7.1 `main()` is 6,131 lines

Measured, not estimated: `Main.cpp:978` opens `main`, and it does not close until the end of a 7,108-line file. The next-longest functions in the file are 89 and 61 lines, so this is not a file of large functions — it is **one function containing the entire game**.

**Is it a problem right now?** Honestly: less than it looks. It works, it is single-player, and the developer is not maintaining a team codebase. But it has two costs that are already being paid:

1. **It is why findings 4.1–4.4 exist.** Five call sites that each had to remember to pass `damage`, none of which the compiler could check, all inside one function too large to hold in your head. That is the exact failure mode a long function produces.
2. **It is the single biggest obstacle to ever writing a test.** Nothing inside `main` can be called from anywhere else. Any automated test of screen state, item movement or the game loop would have to be written against code that cannot be reached.

**If it is split, the safe order** (no tests exist to catch a regression, so this matters): pull out the *pure* things first — the ones that take arguments and return a value with no access to the world — because those cannot change behaviour. Item and slot handling is the obvious first candidate, and it is also where the confirmed bugs are.

### 7.2 The 1.5 MB of documentation

It is genuinely well-maintained — 617 index entries, every one verified to point where it says, no encoding rot, and a script that regenerates every index rather than trusting a hand-written one. That discipline is real and rare.

The cost is equally real: `CLAUDE.md` alone is 31 KB and is attached to *every single turn* of every session. The larger documents are explicitly not meant to be read end to end, which is the right call, but it means the value depends entirely on the indexes staying accurate — which is why `check-index.ps1` is one of the most valuable scripts in the repository.

### 7.3 There is no automated test suite

Not one. The acceptance bar is a clean build at `/W4`, a 45-second soak with no Vulkan validation errors, and the developer playing the game. The project's own documentation states that this "proves it does not crash and almost nothing else", and this audit is the fourth independent confirmation of that: **every finding in §4 and §5 is in code that has passed that bar many times.**

The counter-argument is honest and worth stating: a fragile test harness that a non-C++ developer cannot maintain is worse than none, and the human playtester has genuinely found most of the real bugs. But note what the human *cannot* find: 4.1 destroys items silently, 5.1 is a race that appears once in a thousand minimises, and 5.2 leaves geometry stale in a way that reads as a worldgen bug. **None of those three is discoverable by playing.**

---

> **Still true 2026-08-17, and one corner of it was answered for free.** No test suite was added. What did land is the cheapest possible substitute in the one place it fits: where both sides of a rule are `constexpr`, a `static_assert` proves it at compile time and can never rot. `everyBlockNamed()` now proves every block id has a real name, `slots::roomFor` carries asserts for the stacking rule, `freezingHeight()` asserts the whole lapse-rate derivation, and the drop sweep asserts its own slice length against the terminal velocity. That covers **table totality**, permanently and at zero runtime cost. It does not cover behaviour over time, item conservation across a click, or anything that needs the game to run — which is exactly the `selftest=1` pass §14.4 recommends and nobody has written.

## 8. What is quietly excellent, and must not be broken

> **STILL TRUE.** Nothing here was broken by the 2026-08-18 round, and the compile-time-proof discipline this section praises is the main thing that grew.

Worth naming explicitly, because a review that only lists faults gives a false picture.

- **234 `static_assert`s and 1,860 `constexpr` uses.** This project proves things at compile time as a habit. `foodTablesAgree()` — a check where both sides are `constexpr`, so it can never rot — is exactly the right instinct.
- **The `engine/` ↔ `game/` boundary is genuinely respected.** Zero violations found. Almost every project that writes this rule down breaks it within a month.
- **Threading is confined to four files** and the three purity rules are actually honoured in the code, not just in the documentation. The reviewer who went looking for data races in generation and meshing found none, and said the ownership design was "unusually well" done.
- **`tools/check-models.ps1`.** Measuring 1,792 blocks against the reference's own model JSON, instead of trusting that they look right, is the single best tool in the repository. It exists because a bed cost four playtest rounds — which is the correct response to being burned twice.
- **Derived indexes over hand-written ones.** The documentation applies the project's own commonest bug shape ("a value kept somewhere other than the thing that owns it") to its own prose.
- **`kChunkFormatVersion` is used honestly**, including the hard lesson written next to it about why holding it back to save a world costs more than it saves.
- **The save path uses a temp file and an atomic rename.** A crash mid-write cannot corrupt a chunk.

## 9. Repo hygiene and shipping risk

> **RETIRED (9.1) / OPEN (9.2, 9.3).** The git-history asset argument is retired by the developer's ruling. The project is still named `VoxelGame`, and it still cannot be built into a shippable product by anyone but this machine.

### 9.1 Mojang-derived images are in the permanent git history

`.gitignore` was written carefully to keep reference art out — `reference/` is excluded, `*-preview.png` is excluded, `*-shot.png` is excluded. It worked for 662 MB of assets, none of which is tracked.

But **7 loose PNG files sit in the repository root and are committed**:

| File | Size |
|---|---|
| `m27a.png` | 1,093,041 bytes |
| `m27b.png` | 1,093,628 bytes |
| `bell.png` | 773,786 bytes |
| `b-front.png` | 616,085 bytes |
| `bell-crop.png` | 52,118 bytes |
| `sheepref.png` | 43,212 bytes |
| `refsheep.png` | 31,288 bytes |

By their names, several are crops and screenshots of the reference — `refsheep`, `sheepref`, `bell-crop`, `b-front` are working images from texture and model sessions. They are ~3.7 MB of the 11.2 MB repository, and being in history means removing them later requires rewriting history.

**This is not urgent and it is not a crisis** — the repository is private and unpushed. But it is worth deciding deliberately rather than by accident, and it is much cheaper to deal with now than after the project is ever shared. The developer's own rule is that reference pixels never enter the build; this is the one place they entered the *repository*.

### 9.2 The name is still `VoxelGame`

`CMakeLists.txt` says so with a comment admitting it is a placeholder. `TIMELINE.md` lists it under Open Decisions as "needed before M35, harmless until then". That remains true — just noting the clock is now closer than it was.

### 9.3 The game cannot be built into a shippable product by anyone but this machine

Not a bug, but worth stating: a stranger cloning the repository gets a game of white cubes in silence, because `reference/` is 662 MB and correctly excluded. Everything a player would see or hear is currently staged from it. See §3.

## 10. Suggested order of work

> **SUPERSEDED by §E.** This ordering predates the 2026-08-18 round and most of it is closed. Use **§E** for what is actually left.

Deliberately ordered by *cost of leaving it* rather than by interest. **The top three are all one afternoon's
work between them and they are the difference between "a bug" and "the player loses their evening."**

1. **Autosave, and save on the crash path (§11.2 #2).** The single worst thing in this audit. All non-terrain
   state — inventory, chests, furnaces, stowboxes, creatures — is written exactly once, after the frame loop.
   A driver hiccup, a `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`, or Task Manager loses all of it, *while terrain that unloaded
   mid-session is kept*. That asymmetry is worse than losing everything: it leaves the chest standing there,
   empty. A timed autosave plus calling the same routine from the `catch` is about an hour.
2. **The `damage` field bugs (§4.1, §4.2, §4.4, §11.2 #1).** Eight call sites, one root cause. They silently
   destroy player items today, and **the death-drop path is one of them**, which means durability is
   effectively an optional system right now. §11.2's `dropStack(...)` suggestion closes all eight at once and
   makes the ninth impossible — that is the right shape of fix, not eight one-line patches.
3. **Dropped items have no delta clamp, no unloaded-chunk guard and no swept test (§11.2 #3).** Every other
   moving thing in the game has at least two of the three. Presents as "my drops vanish sometimes", which is
   unreproducible and gets blamed on the despawn timer.
4. **A skeleton's arrow cannot hit the player at all (§13.1).** Four archer species have no path to player
   damage whatsoever. `certain`, and it means a whole combat archetype currently does nothing.
5. **Crops never grow at or above y=32 (§12.1).** One missing `coord.y * Chunk::kSize +` term. Any hillside
   or rooftop farm is dead, and the wasted random tick lands on an unrelated cell lower down.
6. **Villager job, bed and bell claims are not saved (§13.3).** Villages look right after a reload and never
   function again — and the workstation reads as free, so a second villager duplicates the trade.
7. **A mob's arrow that clips a creature is blamed on the player (§13.2).** Turns your own wolves, villagers
   and iron golems hostile through no action of yours.
8. **Tool tiers are unenforced for two entire block runs (§13.5).** Anvils, beacons, spawners and the waxed
   copper family drop to a bare hand. Same shape as the "about two hundred blocks" bug already paid for once.
9. **The inventory cannot swap two tools (§11.2 #4).** Not data loss, but a player rearranging their tools
   will conclude the inventory is broken, and it fires constantly.
10. **The explosion container cleanup (§4.3, §11.2 #6).** Small, and it leaves ghost state keyed at a world
    position that a later-placed container inherits.
11. **The stale-mesh revision bug (§5.2).** Reads as a worldgen fault when it happens, which is the worst
    kind of bug — it sends you looking in the wrong place.
12. **The minimise-path GPU free (§5.1).** Rare, but it is a use-after-free on the GPU: a crash you will
    never reproduce on demand.
13. **Per-pass GPU timestamps (§11.3 #1).** Not an optimisation — a *measurement*, and the one that turns
    every other rendering decision from a guess into an answer. Do this before any of §6.
14. **Chunk compression (§6 B-New-1)** and **flush-before-rename (§11.2 #8).** Cheap, and both get cheaper
    the sooner they are done. Pair the second with the autosave work.
15. **Decide the art plan (§3, §14.1) and write `tools/package.ps1` as a legal gate (§14.7b).** Neither is
    code you would enjoy, and they are the two things standing between this and something a stranger can
    legally play. The packaging gate should *fail the build* if any `*-reference*` path is in the payload —
    and note that `assets/textures/hud.png` is Mojang's and ships unconditionally today.
16. **Everything in §6 that has a measurement attached** — but only *after* running the measurement.

**Deliberately not recommended: starting M30 (ray tracing).** It is marked Experimental, it adds to the pile
of things that must be settings, and nothing in front of the player is blocked on it. Two independent
reviewers reached that conclusion without being asked to — and one added the sharper point that **tuning ray
tracing against art that will not ship means tuning it twice**.

**The one piece of new code most worth writing:** the `selftest=1` startup pass described in §14.4 — stack
conservation, table totality, and block-entity cleanup coverage. No framework, no dependency, same shape as
the `worldgen_probe` and `block_probe` that already exist and are already trusted. It would have caught
items 2, 3, 8 and 9 above in a single run, and it targets precisely the class of bug a human playtester
provably cannot see. Pair it with one new rule in `CLAUDE.md`: **when a temporary probe finds a bug, it
becomes a permanent check instead of being deleted.** Four probes have been written and thrown away, and
between them they found 29 real faults.
